Required to hold a valid California driver's license, have a driving record that is in accordance with local policies/procedures, and/or enroll in the California Employer Pull Notice Program
Bachelor’s degree in Zoology, Biology, Physiology or related science or equivalent education and experience that would equate to a Bachelor’s degree.
Experience and skills to conduct behavioral and physiological studies in the lab to assess sub-lethal effects and impairments in fish.

Experience operating a vehicle in off-road situations on rough terrain and to operate a vehicle while towing heavy equipment, vessel, or live fish transport trailers that can be longer than the tow vehicle.
Experience with fish husbandry of native and/or threatened California fish species, such as sturgeon, salmonids, and Delta smelt.

Experience with health and safety regulations, policies, and techniques. Knowledge of laws federal and state pertaining to occupational safety, environmental and public health. This includes knowledge of the dangers and safe handling of compressed Oxygen cylinders and gauges.
Experience with water quality equipment and testing methods; temperature, salinity, Redox, NH3/NH4, NO2, NO3, turbidity, etc.

The Fangue Lab is part of the Department or Wildlife, Fish, & Conservation Biology. The goal of the lab is to utilize state-of-the-art technologies to understand fundamental physiological, behavioral, and ecological processes. Incumbent participates in achievement of a wide-range of research goals which include providing high-quality support for aquatic animal physiological experiments, culture of both fish and invertebrate species, disease identification and treatment, and fundamentals of testing and monitoring in aquatic environments with attention to detail in order to ensure integrity of results. This position will assist in the planning and implementation of experiments, laboratory analyses, and some field operations for the Fangue Lab and its collaborators to understand the key requirements of California native fishes and fishes more broadly. Expected to develop collaborative relationships with colleagues, and to provide leadership and facilitate teamwork. Oversee live animal collection and husbandry, and assist supervisors in maintaining safety programs including laboratory and field safety ensuring compliance with Federal, State, County, and UC regulations.
Knowledge of statistical analysis using R statistical programming language.
Fundamental knowledge of fish health and disease prevention.
Knowledge of lab equipment including Osomometers, flame photometer, autoclaves, drying ovens, PCR, titrations, digital gas mixing valves.
Strong diagnostic skills in identifying problem to ensure timely action is taken to prevent animal loss.
